QF.id: XC Case Studies and Practical Application_15

question.text: Nisha, a part-time investment adviser, currently has 70 clients. A new prospective client approaches her. Under SEBI regulations, Nisha should:

answer.text: Accept the new client since the limit is 100 for part-time IAs
Accept the new client as she has room for 5 more clients under the 75-client limit
Refuse the new client as she is at her maximum capacity
Accept the client but charge a premium fee since she is near capacity

explanation.text: The Logic: Part-time investment advisers are capped at 75 clients in total at any point in time. With 70 existing clients, Nisha can accept up to 5 more before she reaches the cap, so she can onboard this prospective client. The Trap: The cap for part-time IAs is 75, not 100. She is not at capacity yet with 70 clients. Charging a premium fee because of capacity is not a regulatory concept; the 300-client / INR 3 crore threshold is what triggers a mandatory transition for full-time individual IAs, not part-timers.
